headline: Coal Falls Below 50% in China's Power Mix for First Time
meta_description: China's electricity generation crossed a historic milestone in early 2026 as coal dropped below 50% while renewables surged to 41.2%.
summary_short: In the first half of 2026, coal fell below 50% of China's electricity generation for the first time, while renewable energy rose to 41.2%.
body:
Coal has fallen below 50 percent of China's electricity generation for the first time in the first half of 2026—a historic shift for the world's biggest coal consumer. The drop marks a genuine turning point in the country's energy landscape, one that seemed distant just years ago.

Renewable energy sources surged to fill much of the gap, reaching 41.2 percent of generation during the same period. This combination reveals a real transition underway: not just coal declining, but alternatives genuinely stepping in to meet demand.

For a nation long synonymous with coal power, crossing this threshold signals that the world's largest economy is reshaping its relationship with fossil fuels—driven by economics, technology, and urgency alike.
quick_facts: Coal dropped below 50% of China's electricity for the first time in H1 2026
Renewables rose to 41.2% of China's electricity generation
China is the world's biggest coal consumer
